text.p: Electrical fittings company Clipsal Industries Holdings Ltd said its recent share placement was part of parent company Gold Peak Industries Holdings Ltd's move to "deconsolidate its two major subsidiaries".
Clipsal said earlier in June that it had placed out nine million new shares at US$3.79 each to raise net proceeds of US$33.5 million.
Gold Peak had also sold three million existing Clipsal shares to Peregrine Brokerage Ltd at US$3.79 each. After the exercise Gold Peak's stake in Clipsal fell to 46 percent from 50.1 percent.
The funds raised were also to finance Clipsal's expansion in Asia, Clipsal chairman Victor Lo said.
"For a while the Gold Peak group wanted to restructure...in the sense we wanted to deconsolidate our two largest subsidiaries -- GP Batteries and Clipsal," Lo said.
GP Batteries International Ltd also in June placed out seven million shares to instititional investors and three million shares to retail invetsors.
Lo said the listing of GP Batteries and Clipsal on the Stock Exchange of Singapore had helped the group to raise funds and expand rapidly in the last few years.
"But while these major subsidiaries remain subsidiaries, meaning we (Gold Peak) own more than 50 percent, we also have to consolidate the gearing. There is a chain effect on gearing."
Although the units were lowly geared now, whenever they borrowed more money, it would push up the gearing of Gold Peak.

After Gold Peak shareholders approved lowering the subsidiary holdings below 50 percent, the group decided to take advantage of favourable demand for Clipsal and GP Batteries and placed out shares, Lo said.
He added that Gold Peak and its now associate companies GP Batteries and Clipsal were aiming to maintain low gearing.
K.W. Chau, Clipsal managing director, said Clipsal shares were placed out to institutional investors in Singapore, Europe and the United States.

The proceeds are being used to expand research and development and testing laboratories, and to develop more products, fund new equipment, and for new joint ventures and facilities being planned in China.
Lo said he did not see Gold Peak reducing its stakes further in either Clipsal or GP Batteries.
In Clipsal's case, the funds from the placement would be sufficient for its expanion in the foreseeable future.
"As long as interest rates remain at current levels, there is room to go to bank borrowings for other expansions," Lo said.
